verdict.rationale: Restate splits orchestration from execution. The Restate Server holds the journal and orchestration, while services run in your own infrastructure as containers, Lambdas, VMs or Kubernetes pods. A vendor-managed option exists as Restate Cloud or BYOC, a managed region in your own cloud account. However, the claim that data stays inside your network rests only on a one-line BYOC mention: with Restate Cloud the journal and state live with the vendor, and the vendor server must reach your services. Missing for 10: detailed BYOC docs on data residency and network boundaries, private connectivity between the managed control plane and self-hosted workers, independent corroboration of BYOC deployments.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I run workers in my own infrastructure while the vendor manages the orchestration control plane — code and data stay inside my network

citations.quote: Services run in your infrastructure as containers, serverless functions, VMs, or Kubernetes pods
You can use Restate Cloud, run a managed Restate region in your cloud account with Restate BYOC, or operate Restate yourself.
the restate server does handle the durable execution journal / orchestration, while the user code runs in a separate process, we don't host the code ourselves at the moment
Only Restate needs to be able to make requests to your services. The Restate Server will proxy all requests for these services.
